Note: run it only on model files you trust, since a .gltf file can point to extra buffer or texture URLs that get fetched. The --transform option pulls in sharp, whose install downloads a prebuilt image library.

Check the Portal before paying.
tools.Safety reason: Claude (the wiki code review at commit 9a56be3, 2026-11-01): caution. Safety 8/10 in a container (Hermes Cloud agent or Hermes's Docker image), 5/10 on a PC's default local backend for any bot that reads web, X or YouTube content, because its own SECURITY.md says the OS is the only security boundary. Good: unknown chat users denied by default, dangerous commands denied in cron by default, no telemetry by default, explicit updates on the stable channel, locked dependencies. Risks: `hermes debug share` uploads message text to a public paste site; plugins.auto_apply; unreviewed third-party skills and plugins. Earlier, a review bot (official README, 2026-10-31): installs by piping a script into PowerShell (iex (irm …)) or bash; an autonomous agent with shell, file and browser tools; hermes setup can import other agents' configs (~/.claude, ~/.cursor); Nous Portal sign-in is OAuth with paid usage; its bundled uv.exe is often flagged by antivirus (vendor says false positive).
tools.Install notes:
Caution: read the Safety reason and ask the user before installing.
Windows: in PowerShell run `iex (irm https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/install.ps1)` (official README); it installs under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes`. A separate MSIX package is in the official installation docs (https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/getting-started/installation).
Android: Termux only, from the signed APT repository in the official Termux guide (https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/getting-started/termux), not the desktop installer.
Hermes: after installing run `hermes setup`, or `hermes setup --portal` to sign in to Nous Portal.
Hermes tips : `hermes plugins search <name>` searches the plugin catalog (replace <name> with a word for the plugin you want); `hermes sessions optimize` shrinks state.db and is documented as non-destructive. `hermes plugins install homeassistant --enable` is the official Nous plugin but gives the agent smart-home control, so enable it deliberately. `hermes tools --summary` is not in the docs (unconfirmed).
Setup rules (the wiki code review @9a56be3, 2026-11-01): run it in a container (the Hermes Cloud agent or Hermes's Docker image) for any bot that reads web, X or YouTube content, not on a PC's default local backend. Early/active-development editor with file-editing automation and updater code; use disposable copies and backups. No tracking SDK found in targeted runtime scan; this does NOT establish zero telemetry. Update machinery uses pinned external craft-libs dependency (Cargo.toml); consent/defaults and dependency internals not fully reviewed. Do not label updates silent or claim isolation. Agent file access is not a security sandbox. No blanket execution/permission grants; untrusted documents and tool output can carry prompt injection. Update source: crates/ui-egui/src/updates_ui.rs:8:use craft_update:\:updater\::\{Action, Status, Updater\}; Additional evidence: crates/zotero/src/bridge.rs:31 external Zotero reference; crates/mcp/src/backend.rs local client implementation, transport defaults not fully reviewed.
tools.Install notes: CAUTION: not installed. Ask the user before any install. Official Windows standalone/portable download: https://getartcraft.com/apps/wordcraft. Prefer one standalone app before a suite launcher. Compatible local MCP/CLI required; see repo README for app-specific commands. Windows binaries advertised; integration not tested. Hermes compatibility untested (generic MCP candidate only). claude.ai browser cannot directly execute these local programs; no Android-native support verified. Keep agent approvals on; no YOLO/skip-permissions; non-sensitive file copies, backups, no production keys; review update settings and optional remote/model/provider features before enabling. No install, build, test or repo script run.

tools.Name: yt-dlp
tools.Safety reason: Claude (code read, b77c930 = 2026.10.26, 2026-11-01): caution, 6/10. No telemetry; releases GPG-signed. Risks for agents: config files auto-load from the current folder, ~/.config and /etc (a config can set --exec, --proxy, plugin dirs) unless --ignore-config; Python plugins auto-import from site-packages/sys.path unless YTDLP_NO_PLUGINS=1; --cookies-from-browser decrypts every cookie in the browser, and yt-dlp's bot-check error tells agents to use it; 5 high-severity injection advisories in 2026 plus a certifi MITM warning for old executables, so stay current. Platform risk: YouTube ToS forbids downloading/automated access; account cookies risk bans; re-uploading others' clips brings strikes. Live test from a Claude cloud machine (2026-11-01): Instagram reels download without login; TikTok works with the curl_cffi extra; YouTube gives metadata and captions but the video download gets HTTP 403 (cloud-IP block). Earlier: a review bot inferred caution (Instagram/TikTok terms); Grok uses it in a project reel breakdowns (2026-10-30/31).
tools.Install notes:
Caution: read the Safety reason and ask the user before installing.
Claude Code: use the a download skill skill (user's account skill): pinned venv with pip install --only-binary=\:all\: "yt-dlp[default,pin,pin-deno,pin-curl-cffi]==2026.10.26". Cloud projects must allow instagram.com, *.instagram.com, *.cdninstagram.com, *.fbcdn.net (TikTok: tiktok.com, *.tiktok.com, *.tiktokcdn.com, *.tiktokcdn-us.com, *.tiktokv.com; YouTube: youtube.com, *.youtube.com, *.googlevideo.com, *.ytimg.com) under Network access.
10.26" (wheel sha256 a05c5b5d8562f7e8a62f5334348b406af4930d56d3a65f8021d14af0e22339ae). One Unix user per bot.
Every run: YTDLP_NO_PLUGINS=1 yt-dlp --ignore-config --no-config-locations --no-plugin-dirs --no-remote-components --no-cookies --no-cookies-from-browser --no-exec --no-exec-before-download --no-playlist -t sleep -P <own folder> -o "%(id)s.%(ext)s" -- URL
Standalone binary check: sha256sum must equal 767ba9dce7052aa196f8b12652f433d76de128ba168966fa84b6394d5e6c6795 (yt-dlp_linux 2026.10.26) or e51e69e89489f199530f13d32a4342da3ddb2cf34842f364603a066db05afbf3 (zipimport yt-dlp), from the GPG-verified SHA2-256SUMS.
Rules: no -U from agents (a human updates within ~1 week of each stable, at once for Security releases); never a project's or any posting account's cookies; on a bot check, 403 or 429 stop and ask for the file; never re-upload third-party clips; only deno as JS runtime; no apt package. Hermes: not needed (its youtube-content skill uses youtube-transcript-api).
Tip (2026-11-01, from the wiki and a review bot): for captions use `--sub-langs en,en-orig`, not `en.*` (that hits HTTP 429). Private posts, Stories, Saved and DMs need sign-in, which the no-cookies rule rules out, so ask the user for the file.
Tip (2026-11-02, from the wiki): from a cloud container, Instagram and TikTok downloads work (TikTok needs the curl_cffi extra), but YouTube gives only info and captions; the video file itself returns HTTP 403, so ask the user for the file.
